messages.content: What is spaced repetition and how do you use it?

Spaced repetition exploits the spacing effect: information reviewed at increasing intervals is retained far more efficiently than massed review (cramming). The forgetting curve (Ebbinghaus) shows that without review, ~70% of new information is lost within 24 hours. Review just before forgetting resets the curve at a higher level each time. Implementation: Anki (spaced repetition software) algorithmically schedules reviews based on your performance ratings. Review cards in the morning (consolidation benefits from overnight sleep). Rate honestly — the algorithm needs accurate data. A well-maintained Anki deck reviewed daily produces near-permanent retention of tens of thousands of facts.
What is the method of loci (memory palace)?

Method of loci: associate information with specific locations in a familiar mental space (your home, a route you know well). To remember a list: mentally walk through the space and place vivid, unusual images at each location. To recall: mentally walk the route again and 'see' the images. Works because spatial memory and episodic memory are among the strongest memory systems — the hippocampus evolved for navigation. Enhancement: make images bizarre, moving, emotionally charged, or obscene — these encode more deeply. World memory champions use this technique to memorise thousands of digits or cards. With practice, anyone can memorise a shuffled deck of cards in under 5 minutes.
How do you learn a complex skill 5x faster than average?

Deliberate practice (Ericsson): not simply doing the thing, but practicing at the edge of current ability with immediate feedback and specific focus on weaknesses. Random practice (drilling what you're already good at) produces comfort, not growth. Principles: (1) Identify the exact sub-skills and practice them in isolation. (2) Get feedback at the highest possible rate — a coach who corrects in real time beats solo practice. (3) Mental representations: build increasingly sophisticated mental models of what excellence looks like, then compare your performance to that model. (4) 90 minutes of focused deliberate practice produces more improvement than 4 hours of unfocused practice.
